newsitem.title: USA: J. Ray McDermott revises fiscal 97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: J. Ray McDermott revises fiscal 97 earnings.

text.p: J. Ray McDermott, S.A. said on Tuesday that it had changed from the equity method of accounting to the cost method for its investment in its HeereMac joint venture with the Heerema Offshore Construction Group and this has resulted in a revision to its fiscal 1997 earnings.
The company said in a statement that in the 12 months ended March 31, the net loss has been revised to $19.0 million, or $0.47 a share, from $11.3 million, or $0.28 a share.
The net loss for the quarter ended March 31, 1997 has been revised to $45.5 million, or $1.12 a share, from $58.6 million, or $1.44 a share.
J. Ray is majority owned by McDermott International Inc.

The company is conducting an audit into alleged wrongdoing by a number of former employees of J. Ray McDermott and McDermott International and this centers on possible anti-competitive activity in the heavy-lift barge service business of J. Ray McDermott and HeereMac.
In July, McDermott International received an informal request from the Securities and Exchange Commission for the voluntary production of documents relating, in part, to HeereMac.
If the allegations are true, grand jury proceedings could result in civil and/or criminal liability for McDermott International and J. Ray McDermott.
